item.title: ASP.NET Core Large File Upload Limit Configuration: IIS, Kestrel, and Application Settings
item.description:
“ASP.NET Core Large File Upload Limit Configuration: IIS, Kestrel, and Application Settings”

When handling file uploads or large data payloads in ASP.NET Core applications, developers frequently encounter limitations on the maximum request body size. These restrictions are imposed at multiple layers: by the hosting environment (like IIS), by the built-in web server (Kestrel), and within the application’s configuration itself via middleware settings. Overcoming these hurdles requires coordinated adjustments across these areas.

item.title: Resolving CORS Configuration Across Various ASP.NET Core Versions
item.description:
“Resolving CORS Configuration Across Various ASP.NET Core Versions”

Enabling Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) is a frequent necessity when building modern web applications, especially when a frontend application (like Angular or React) resides on a different domain or port than the ASP.NET Core backend API. Different versions of ASP.NET Core employ slightly varied setups for middleware pipeline registration and service configuration. How do developers correctly set up CORS policies for specific application needs across these versions?

item.title: Custom Authorization in ASP.NET Core: Strategies and Code Examples
item.description:
“Custom Authorization in ASP.NET Core: Strategies and Code Examples”

Implementing robust authorization in ASP.NET Core applications ensures that users only access resources and perform actions for which they have explicit permission. While the framework provides built-in authorization mechanisms, there are numerous scenarios where custom authorization logic is necessary. This exploration delves into various strategies and provides practical code examples to help you implement effective custom authorization in your ASP.NET Core projects.
